answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped until it completes a sequence of randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked against later, independently sampled outcomes. A real participant can build a consistent record; a swarm of fresh identities must spend time and compute on every account, while coordinated agents risk repeating patterns that reveal shared control. The sparrow test can be one small task, but the kernel is the costly accumulation of verified history, not a relic credential that can simply be copied. This raises the price of sybils without assuming identity checks are foolproof.
